_comment: XC-3 Phase 0b ledger of every src/app/api/**/route.ts that imports the RLS-bypassing service-role client (@/lib/supabase-admin or a relative path to lib/supabase-admin). This list RATCHETS DOWN ONLY: as Phase 2/3 migrate read routes onto the RLS-scoped supabase-server client, their entries are pruned here in the same PR. A NEW admin-importing route that is absent from this ledger FAILS src/__tests__/api-admin-client-allowlist.test.ts (which re-derives the detected set from source with the same import matcher). 263 -> 264: GenAI Phase 5a outcome-prediction cross-student read (service-role after canAccessStudent). 264 -> 265 (2026-07-29, architect-reviewed): P0-1 quota display/enforcement gap — src/app/api/usage/daily/route.ts reads the caller's OWN daily quota from get_plan_limit(), the SAME authority check_and_record_usage() enforces from. Service-role is REQUIRED here, not convenience: migration 20260729130400 §5 (re-asserting 20260516040000/20260516050000) REVOKEs EXECUTE ON public.get_plan_limit(uuid, text) FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated, so an RLS-scoped session cannot call it at all. Bounded surface: one STABLE read-only RPC + one own-row SELECT on student_daily_usage, both keyed on the SESSION-derived auth.studentId (students.auth_user_id = caller) — no studentId is ever accepted from the request, so there is no cross-student path. Read-only: no insert/update/increment/grant; the hard gate stays checkAndIncrementQuota -> check_and_record_usage in /api/foxy. Gated by authorizeRequest() on 'foxy.chat'/'quiz.attempt' (both granted to the student role by 20260612123200); EVERY unrecognised ?feature= — inherited Object.prototype keys (toString/constructor/valueOf/hasOwnProperty/__proto__/isPrototypeOf/propertyIsEnumerable/toLocaleString) included — is rejected 400 BEFORE authorizeRequest and before any service-role call. Architect-verified against shipped source 2026-07-29: FEATURE_PERMISSION is a new Map<string, string> (route.ts:82-85) and the guard is typeof permission !== 'string' (route.ts:95-100); Map.prototype.get consults no prototype chain, so inherited keys are unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a guard each new call site must remember, and no caller-controlled string can reach get_plan_limit's generous ai_calls_total ELSE arm. HISTORY (CLOSED — recorded so the fix is not re-litigated, not as an open item): the pre-ship draft used a plain object literal typed Record<string, string>, where inherited keys returned truthy and slipped past the !permission guard. The impact was BROADER than first recorded here: a student caller got an unhandled 500 (rbac.ts:785 calls .split() on the non-string permission in the deny branch, above the try), but a super_admin caller took the isSuperAdmin short-circuit at rbac.ts:779-780, which skips the permission check entirely, so a prototype key DID reach get_plan_limit and land in its ai_calls_total ELSE arm. That path additionally required the caller to own a student row, and get_plan_limit is a read-only STABLE function, so the over-generous number was DISPLAY-only and never raised the ENFORCED cap in check_and_record_usage. Both paths are closed by the Map plus typeof guard, pinned by 4 tests covering 8 prototype keys. Response is 4 ints + 1 bool, no PII (P13). RATCHET-DOWN PATH: add an auth.uid()-anchored SECURITY DEFINER wrapper get_my_plan_limit(p_feature text) GRANTed to authenticated, move the route to the RLS-scoped client, and prune this entry. Do NOT instead GRANT EXECUTE on get_plan_limit(uuid, text) to authenticated — it takes p_student_id and performs no auth.uid() check, so that would expose every student's cap to every authenticated user. Pinned by REG-213 (P8/P9). 268 -> 269 (2026-08-02, architect-reviewed): Mock Exam Runner v2 autosave — new save-only route src/app/api/exams/papers/[id]/autosave/route.ts. Service-role is REQUIRED here, not convenience: mock_test_attempts RLS (20260520000008) keys mock_test_attempts_update_own/select_own on student_id = auth.uid() directly (student_id REFERENCES auth.users(id)), but this entire route family — this route's already-ledgered siblings [id]/start/route.ts and [id]/submit/route.ts (see 'Phase 2.2 mock-exam remediation' above) — resolves and filters on authorizeRequest()'s studentId, which is students.id, a DIFFERENT uuid than auth.uid(). An RLS-scoped client (supabase-server/supabase-route) filtering .eq('student_id', studentId) with that same studentId would be silently zero-rowed by the auth.uid()-keyed policy — indistinguishable from the route's own legitimate persisted:false no-op branch, i.e. a silent persistence failure, not a security win. Bounded surface: a single UPDATE scoped to id + student_id + exam_paper_id + status='in_progress', touching only the pre-existing client_metadata jsonb column — NEVER score_percent/raw_score/xp_earned/status/submitted_at (enforced by the route's own field-level write shape, not by a WHERE filter). Gated by the same exam.view authorizeRequest() permission as all three siblings; student_id/exam_paper_id/status are app-supplied filters only, never derived from a request-controlled join, so there is no cross-student read/write path. RATCHET-DOWN PATH: reconcile student_id semantics across the whole [id]/{start,submit,autosave} family (store auth.uid() consistently, matching the table's own RLS design, or add an auth.uid()-anchored SECURITY DEFINER autosave RPC mirroring submit_mock_test_attempt), then move all three routes to the RLS-scoped client together — flagged for architect/backend follow-up, out of scope for this PR. 269 -> 268 (2026-08-03, architect-approved in the P1 verifyCronAuth batch): src/app/api/cron/daily/route.ts DELETED — it was a deprecated alias for /api/cron/daily-cron, scheduled by nothing and carrying only deprecation telemetry; its entry is pruned in the SAME change so the ledger ratchets DOWN, not drifts. 268 -> 265 (2026-08-03, P2-7b): teacher/messages/{route,threads,threads/[id]/messages} migrated to SECURITY DEFINER RPCs under RLS (createSupabaseServerClient), pruned in the same change so the ledger ratchets DOWN. 268 -> 269 (2026-08-05, Foxy North-Star Phase 5 lane U10): NEW route src/app/api/v1/leaderboard/me/route.ts legitimately uses the admin client. Service-role read of the get_leaderboard_percentile RPC scoped to the SESSION-derived studentId (auth.uid()-resolved; ?student_id ignored) after authorizeRequest('leaderboard.view'); returns caller-owned percentile band + PII-free neighbours. Ratchet-down path: replace with an auth.uid()-anchored SECURITY DEFINER RPC then move to the RLS-scoped client. 269 -> 268 (2026-08-06, P1 health consolidation, commit eaa7e1ab): src/app/api/health/route.ts migrated to a pure-liveness endpoint (no downstream dependency probes, no service-role reads) and its ledger entry is pruned in the SAME change so the ledger ratchets DOWN, not drifts. 268 -> 267 (2026-08-10): src/app/api/v2/student/profile/route.ts migrated to the RLS-scoped request client (createSupabaseRouteClient) behind the new learners repository module; own-row read is served by the students_select_merged policy (auth_user_id = auth.uid()), so service-role is no longer required. Pruned in the SAME change so the ledger ratchets DOWN. 267 -> 269 (2026-08-11, leaderboard SEV1 Pattern-B repair): TWO new routes legitimately require service-role. (a) src/app/api/v1/leaderboard/titles/route.ts — student_titles has RLS ENABLED with EXACTLY ONE policy, "Service role full access on student_titles" (baseline :20003); there is NO student SELECT policy at all, so an RLS-scoped client reads 0 rows for every caller and the "My Titles" tab was permanently empty. Bounded surface: one SELECT on student_titles filtered .eq(student_id, auth.studentId) — the SESSION-derived id; a ?student_id param is ignored. Own-data only, no cross-student path. (b) src/app/api/v1/leaderboard/streaks/route.ts — a peer streak leaderboard; challenge_streaks RLS is own-row-only (challenge_streaks_student_select, baseline :20607) and students_select_merged is own/teacher-of/guardian-of, so a cross-student board is structurally impossible under RLS (the page previously read it from the BROWSER and rendered the single returned row as a "Top Streaks" board). Bounded surface: two capped SELECTs (challenge_streaks >= visibility threshold, then students by id IN the surviving set), projected through an explicit P13 whitelist — peers get rank/student_id/name/grade/current_streak plus badges already implied by the exposed current_streak; best_streak, avatar_url, school, city, last_challenge_date and the mercy-day counters never leave the server. Gated by authorizeRequest(leaderboard.view) / (progress.view_own for titles). RATCHET-DOWN PATH: add auth.uid()-anchored SECURITY DEFINER RPCs (get_my_titles(), get_streak_leaderboard(p_limit)) GRANTed to authenticated, mirroring get_class_leaderboard, then move both routes to the RLS-scoped client and prune these entries. NOTE the sibling src/app/api/v1/leaderboard/my-class/route.ts added in the same change is deliberately NOT here: it uses the RLS-scoped createSupabaseRouteClient (class_students own-enrollment policy + the already-SECURITY-DEFINER get_class_leaderboard RPC granted to authenticated). 269 -> 270 (2026-08-11, support first-response SLA): NEW route src/app/api/internal/admin/support/metrics/route.ts. Service-role is REQUIRED here, not convenience, and the RLS-scoped alternative was checked FIRST and rejected on evidence: NEITHER table this route reads has ANY operator/admin/support-role SELECT policy. support_tickets has exactly two SELECT policies, both requester-anchored -- 'Users can read own tickets' (email = the caller's own auth.users email OR student_id IN the caller's own students, baseline :20262) and support_tickets_self_select (student_id IN own students, baseline :22378). support_ticket_replies (20260814000012) has exactly three policies: _owner_select (authenticated, is_internal=false AND own student-filed ticket), _owner_insert, and _service_role_all; that migration's own policy comment states the design explicitly -- 'Operator replies, internal notes, edits and redactions all go through the service-role client, which bypasses RLS. Authorisation for those writes is enforced in the route by authorizeAdmin()/authorizeRequest(), NOT here.' So an operator holding support.view_tickets, reading through createSupabaseRouteClient, would see ONLY the tickets that operator personally filed. The failure mode is the reason this is disqualifying rather than merely degraded: this route exists to make the newly-published 2-business-day SLA falsifiable, and over a near-empty row set it would return breach_count 0 and meeting_promise true -- i.e. it would silently certify that we are meeting the promise PRECISELY BECAUSE it cannot see the breaches. A metric that fails toward 'all clear' is worse than no metric. The RLS-scoped client is therefore not a second line of defense here, it is a silent-zero. Consistency: the sibling operator console src/app/api/internal/admin/support/route.ts (ticket list, thread view, status PATCH, operator reply POST) is already in this ledger, reads the SAME two tables, and is gated by the SAME authorizeRequest('support.view_tickets') code; splitting one operator surface across two clients would buy nothing. BOUNDED SURFACE: read-only, no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/RPC of any kind. Exactly three query shapes, all hard-capped -- (1) support_tickets created inside a 1..365-day window, LIMIT 5000; (2) still-open support_tickets of any age, LIMIT 2000; (3) support_ticket_replies chunked by ticket_id IN (<=200) with is_internal=false AND author_role IN (operator,admin,system), for the ticket ids returned by (1)+(2) only. Both query params (days, queue_limit) are Number.parseInt + clamped to fixed ranges before use; no caller-supplied string reaches any filter, and there is no id/tenant parameter at all, so there is no cross-tenant or request-steered read path. P13 FIELD WHITELIST (the load-bearing justification): support_tickets carries email, user_name, subject, message, device_info and admin_notes -- NONE is selected. The ticket SELECT list is pinned to the single TICKET_COLUMNS constant 'id, category, status, created_at, resolved_at' and the reply SELECT to 'ticket_id, created_at, author_role'. No message body and no author identity (no author_user_id, no author name) is ever read, so no reply text can reach the response even by accident. The response is aggregate counts/percentiles plus a work queue of (ticket_id, category, status, created_at, age); ticket UUIDs only. Errors return a generic 'Internal error' body rather than the PostgREST string, which would otherwise echo the ticket-id IN-list back to the caller. Nothing is logged and nothing is written to audit_logs -- read-only aggregate, no operator action to audit. RATCHET-DOWN PATH (concrete): add a SECURITY DEFINER RPC public.get_support_first_response_metrics(p_days int, p_queue_limit int) RETURNS jsonb that opens with IF NOT public.check_permission(auth.uid(), 'support.view_tickets') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION -- check_permission(uuid, text) already exists SECURITY DEFINER in the baseline (:1973) and resolves user_roles -> role_permissions -> permissions with is_active/expires_at honoured -- projects the same five ticket columns and three reply columns, and is GRANTed EXECUTE to authenticated with EXECUTE REVOKEd from PUBLIC/anon; then move this route to createSupabaseRouteClient and prune this entry. IMPORTANT: the support_ticket_first_response view whose DDL is handed to architect in this route's header comment does NOT achieve that ratchet-down and must not be mistaken for it -- it is declared security_invoker = true and GRANTed to service_role ONLY, so reading it still requires this admin client; it is an ad-hoc-SQL convenience for ops, not the migration path. Do NOT instead add an operator SELECT policy to support_tickets: that would widen RLS over the whole row including email/user_name/subject/message/device_info/admin_notes, trading a narrow server-side column whitelist for broad table-level PII exposure (P13 regression). The RPC keeps the projection server-side where it already is.
